newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar climbs but German rate worries loom.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar climbs but German rate worries loom.

text.p: The dollar climbed against most major currencies on Thursday after German and Swiss central banks left interest rates steady, but market worries of an imminent German rate rise persisted and knocked the U.S. unit off its peaks in late trading.
Most European stock markets, pausing to consolidate recent record highs, were overshadowed by the dollar's steady rise.

The U.S. currency hit a six-year high against the mark near 1.84 and a 43-month peak versus the Swiss franc before investors squared some of their positions and locked in some profits. The dollar also reached its highest level this year against the French franc earlier in the session.

Some dealers said the dollar may have also slipped in late afternoon below 1.83 marks because of fears Germany's central bank may raise rates in two weeks. The jitters were sparked after the Bundesbank said at its last meeting before a four-week summer recess it would have fixed-rate money market operations for two weeks.
By not specifying the rate for the final two weeks of the recess, traders said the Bundesbank could be leaving room for an imminent rate rise.
"They (the Bundesbank) seem to be holding out the threat of a tightening, which could be mark-positive in the days ahead," said Ian Morris, international economist at HSBC James Capel.
Germany's government debt market also reflected fears of higher interest rates. German bund and Euromark prices ended sharply lower as they started pricing in a rate rise soon.
Germany's DAX index, Europe's forerunner in the race this week to all-time highs, closed bourse trading sharply lower. The DAX was weighed by banking shares, which fell on corporate earnings.

Commerzbank AG and Vereinsbank AG fell after first-half results. Commerzbank ended down three marks at 62.00 despite higher-than-expected first-half operating profits, which rose 23.2 percent. Vereinsbank shares closed down 12.50 marks at 102.50 on lower-than-expected earnings. Its operating profit rose 15.2 percent in the first half.
German shares gave up even more ground in after-hours electronic trade. In late European trade, the IBIS DAX was down 39.50 points at 4,345.32, more than 40 points off its mid-afternoon high.

Despite the DAX's slip, traders remained upbeat on the index, saying the dollar's continued strength and money pouring into the market should keep the market buoyed. The strong dollar helps make German goods cheaper abroad, which should boost exports.

Finland's FOX index was the exception among stocks, jumping to an all-time peak earlier in the session after Swedish telecoms group Ericsson reported strong second-quarter earnings and boosted Nokia Ab, Oy.
Ericsson ended up 24 crowns ($3.07) after hitting a year high of 370.00 on impressive first-half results. Ericsson said pre-tax profits gained 44 percent versus a year ago.
Dutch shares, which also posted a record high on Wednesday, lost ground by midday despite an earlier boost from Philips Electronics NV's strong second-quarter earnings.

Philips shares jumped more than eight percent to a year high of 177 guilders ($86.16) before slipping back to end up 5.90 guilders at 171.30. The company said second-quarter net profits from ordinary operations rose to 693 million guilders, outpacing analysts' expectations between 429 and 540 million.
French stocks ended one percent lower, dragged by the Dow Jones Industrial Average's drop into negative territory.
At the European close, the Dow was down 82.69 points at 8,005.67.
The Dow also helped London's FTSE-100 index erase earlier gains made on a smaller-than-expected British May trade deficit.
Imperial Chemical Industries Plc was down 16 pence at 908 after first-half profits fell to 160 million sterling from 367 million last year, as expected.
CURRENCIES AT THE CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.8295 marks and 115.85 yen compared to 1.8235 and 115.73 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 11.6 points at 4,862.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended bourse trading down 70.35 points, or 1.6 percent, at 4,335.74.
PARIS - The CAC-40 finished down 30.00 points at 2,973.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed in London at $322.65 per ounce. Silver was fixed at $4.31 in the afternoon.
